title: Hear, Localize, and Reason: Spatially Aware Scene Understanding for Audio-visual LLMs
claim: A benchmark organizes a capability into a three-level hierarchy, from perceiving to localizing to relational reasoning, illustrated on one shared scene.
layout: 3 colored panels left-to-right, numbered stages, QA boxes under a shared scene
description: Three side-by-side rounded panels with green, blue and orange borders. Each is numbered and titled: 1 Spatial hearing, 2 Spatial grounding, 3 Spatial relational reasoning. Panel 1 shows a rendered bedroom from the agent's view. A ringing alarm clock, a baby, a dog and a piano appear in it, with a speech bubble saying 'Turn off the alarm!'. Below the room are two green QA boxes, one for sound semantics and one for far-field ASR. Panel 2 is a top-down floor plan of the room. It marks the egocentric and allocentric viewpoints with dashed purple and blue arrows labeled Move, Face and Front-left. Below it are QA boxes giving distance and direction answers. Panel 3 is a column of orange Q&A cards for alarm ringing and man speaking, with small thumbnails. A scene description sits at the bottom. The eye goes first to the large room image on the left.
caption: Overview of HLR-AVSceneQA. We introduce HLR-AVSceneQA, a comprehensive benchmark for spatial audio-visual scene understanding organized around a hear-localize-reason hierarchy. For a queried sound source, the model recognizes what is heard, localizes where it originates in egocentric and allocentric views, and uses the localized source together with visual scene evidence to reason about how it relates to the surrounding scene.
abstract: Audio-visual large language models (AV-LLMs) have made strong progress in multimodal understanding, yet most treat audio as monaural semantic content, limiting their ability to reason about where sounds originate and how they relate to the visual scene. Recent spatial audio-visual studies address parts of this problem, but often focus on specific abilities, such as spatial correspondence or direction and distance reasoning. In this work, we introduce HLR-AVSceneQA, a comprehensive benchmark with a hear-localize-reason hierarchy that evaluates whether models can recognize what is heard, localize sound sources in egocentric and allocentric views, and use these localized sources to reason about how they relate to the visual scene. We further introduce HLR-LLM, which augments a strong audio-visual foundation model with a binaural spatial audio branch alongside its monaural semantic audio pathway. We train HLR-LLM with a curriculum that incorporates final-stage chain-of-thought supervision for multi-step spatial reasoning. Experiments show that existing AV-LLMs remain limited in spatial grounding and relational reasoning, while HLR-LLM substantially improves spatial audio-visual scene understanding without compromising semantic audio-visual perception.
